ratings.why: The request limits assignment to open and in-progress tickets, so a success answer or a refusal that still changes a resolved ticket misleads the client and breaks the API's 409 conflict convention.
Treating {} or a misspelt field as an unassign would quietly change tickets, and the API already promises 400 invalid for malformed bodies and 404 for unknown tickets.
Untrimmed or control-character names split one agent across filters and break the table, so a careful builder applies the same rules as for titles and requesters.
Decision 7 and CONTRIBUTING require every ticket change on the audit log with its actor, and an untraceable reassignment is exactly what the log exists to prevent.
updated is documented as when the ticket last changed and agents sort by it, so an assignment should move it and a no-op should not.
A repeated clear that writes an audit entry or moves updated makes an unchanged ticket look worked, which contradicts the conventions in a smaller way.
Without a template the assignment notification goes dead and the agent is never told, which breaks a stated requirement of the request.
The default dedup key can leave the new owner unnotified after a quick reassignment, a real but timing-dependent gap.
The request asks only that the assigned agent be notified; telling others is optional product taste.
Notifying a self-assigning agent is harmless noise either way and the request says to notify the assigned agent.
The data file names every field it keeps, so assignee is lost at restart unless added, and existing data files must keep loading under decision 8.
Whether the assignee is kept through resolve, close and reopen shapes the filter and the lead's view, and the builder should choose and say so.
The filter should compare the same normalised form assignment stores and refuse impossible values like other filters do, though exact matching is a reasonable default.
A filtered listing whose later pages mix in or skip tickets is a plain defect in a paged API.
matchesFilters in the base uses some, so combined filters list a union contrary to the docs and the request's match-every-filter sentence, which makes the new assignee filter wrong too.
The weekly report reads list --raw columns by position and the README says they must keep their positions, so inserting a column before title breaks it.
Printing null or undefined for an unassigned ticket in the operators' table looks like a fault and should be a clear marker.
show is the full view of one ticket, so leaving the assignee out hides who has it, though the request names only the listing.
A command-line assignee filter was not asked for, and the existing parser already refuses unknown options.
POST and PATCH should keep refusing assignee as an unknown field so assignment cannot bypass its rules, which the base already does by default.
Answering 200 with the ticket like every other change endpoint is what clients expect, a small cost if different.
CONTRIBUTING requires a version bump and changelog section and docs/api.md is what clients read, so a careful builder updates them.
A failed save that leaves memory changed shows an assignment lost at restart, but full or read-only disks are uncommon and the store already handles saves centrally.
The outbox keeps pending events unless a builder deliberately cancels them, so this is speculative.
Assignment has no reason to touch the body-size setting, so guarding it is over-engineering for this request.
The command line must never write the service's data file, and a migration step in show could overwrite live state, though the base gives no reason to add one.
Operators read handoffs from show's history, so assignment entries should appear in order there.
Agents literally named null or names with arrows are unlikely, and making the text unambiguous for them is polish.
